title: Test Coverage and Test Quality
keywords: why coverage percentage alone does not establish correctness
subtopics: Why coverage percentage alone does not establish correctness.
learning_outcomes: Explain what test coverage and test quality contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: line and branch coverage concepts.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Quality comes from several kinds of evidence: unit tests, integration tests, static analysis, coding standards, and repeatable CI. Tests should assert observable behavior and include important failure and boundary cases. In this lesson, focus on line and branch coverage concepts; then compare it with coverage reports. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use test coverage and test quality when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Quality comes from several kinds of evidence: unit tests, integration tests, static analysis, coding standards, and repeatable CI. Tests should assert observable behavior and include important failure and boundary cases. For test coverage and test quality, begin with line and branch coverage concepts. Also distinguish coverage reports; gaps in coverage; mutation-testing concepts. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Test Coverage and Test Quality
content_blocks.code:
<?php
function add(int $a, int $b): int { return $a + $b; }
$actual = add(2, 3);
echo $actual === 5 ? "PASS" : "FAIL";

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Test observable behavior, include boundary cases, and treat static analysis and coverage as evidence rather than proof.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for test coverage and test quality from top to bottom. Start by identifying line and branch coverage concepts, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary inputs and failures can reveal defects that normal examples miss.
common_mistakes.fix: Add empty, invalid, boundary, and failure cases with meaningful assertions.

common_mistakes.why: Tests can become brittle and stop checking real behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Prefer simple unit tests and focused integration tests at actual boundaries.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating coverage as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Executing a line does not guarantee its behavior was asserted.
common_mistakes.fix: Review assertions, relevant branches, edge cases, and regression risk.

summary: Test Coverage and Test Quality is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
Test observable behavior, include boundary cases, and treat static analysis and coverage as evidence rather than proof.
